issues.description: The problem specification requires a method named checkOrderReady() on SealSaloon (UML and textual description). The reference solution instead implements this behavior in a method named processOrders() and does not provide a checkOrderReady() method. This name/signature mismatch between the specification and solution can confuse students about which method to implement and may break automated tests or grading that expect checkOrderReady().
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution and template match the specification: provide a public checkOrderReady() method on SealSaloon with the behavior described in the problem (serving as many queued orders as possible until an order cannot be fulfilled). Either rename processOrders() to checkOrderReady(), or add a public checkOrderReady() that delegates to processOrders(). Ensure the template instructs students to implement checkOrderReady() (method name and signature) to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires a method named checkOrderReady() on SealSaloon to be called from orderMeal() to attempt serving queued orders. In the solution implementation the equivalent behavior is implemented in a method named processOrders(), and orderMeal() calls processOrders() instead. This naming divergence for the same core behavior (checking and serving ready orders) can confuse students trying to map the required API from the problem description to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Use the same method name as specified in the problem: rename processOrders() to checkOrderReady(), and have orderMeal() call checkOrderReady(). Alternatively, add a public checkOrderReady() that delegates to processOrders() so the API matches the problem statement.
